To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Ligand binding pockets occur in all proteins and the number of different pockets is small, and (2) the properties of the pockets are similar in unrelated proteins, and the same properties occur in computer generated proteins, which have not evolved to bind any ligand.

(i) ligand binding pockets are a generic property of proteins; (ii) the number of pockets is small; (iii) pockets in unrelated proteins can have the same properties; (iv) off-target interactions among proteins with diverse functions are inherent; and (v) the small number of pockets is a major factor in off-target interactions.

the number of distinct ligands binding pockets in proteins is small, and that the properties of these pockets in native proteins are very similar to those of pockets generated by computer simulations of protein folding in the absence of ligands and without selection for function.
